text:
Alex: Heads-up — onboarding acme-prod into eu-west-1. Need a VPC/VNet design that includes an interface endpoint (PrivateLink) to our control-plane (redis + metrics), a GPU worker subnet for A100s, and outbound NAT. Two asks: (1) subnet sizing / route precedence for endpoints vs NAT, and (2) quota request for GPUs (p4d/a100) in the new account. Any known blockers?

Mira: @Alex can you paste the planned CIDR + desired AZ spread? Quick notes: on Azure we put private endpoints in a separate subnet with network-policy disabled; on AWS interface endpoints need free IPs in the subnet. For GPU workers, we usually allocate a /21 or /20 depending on fleet size.

Raj: TL;DR on SNAT — avoid single NAT GW for large pod fleets. We burned through SNAT ports during a big rollout. Options: NAT per AZ + EIP pool, or TGW central egress with scaled NATs. If cost is a concern, NAT instances + autoscaling can be cheaper but more operational. Also ensure route tables are specific so endpoint traffic doesn't hairpin to NAT.

Alex: CIDR plan: 10.40.0.0/16. Proposal: private-endpoint subnet 10.40.2.0/28, infra/management 10.40.4.0/22, app subnets 10.40.16.0/21, gpu workers 10.40.8.0/21 (spread across 3 AZs). Is /28 for the interface endpoint OK?

Mira: /28 is fine for interface endpoints, but leave a couple of IPs spare for future endpoints and LB ENIs. On AWS the interface endpoints create ENIs — make sure the subnet has enough IP capacity. Also tag subnets correctly: e.g., `kubernetes.io/cluster/<name>=shared` and internal-use tags.

Raj: For route precedence: add specific routes for endpoint ENI CIDRs or rely on interface endpoints (they're local). Main rule: do NOT point 0.0.0.0/0 to NAT in the subnet where endpoints live. Instead, have worker route table -> NAT and endpoint subnet route table -> local. Example route table layout:
```
- endpoint-subnet-rt: local only (no 0.0.0.0/0)
- worker-subnet-rt: 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-gw-azX
- shared-services-rt: 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-gw-azY or tgw
```
Also disable source/dest checks where appropriate and watch for iptables MASQUERADE in k8s if pods egress.

Alex: Good call. For GPU quota: need 10 p4d and 20 a100 (or a mix) in eu-west-1 for initial capacity. Can someone submit the quota request?

Raj: I'll file the AWS case now. Please include expected start date and whether these are burst vs sustained. If these are reserved for Dedicated we may want a capacity commitment.

cloud-ops-bot: Quota case opened: AWS case 1234567890 — requesting 10 p4d instances and 20 a100 (g4dn/a100 family) in eu-west-1. Please add any usage justification in the case. Estimated review 48-72h.

Alex: Thanks. One more: how do we ensure PrivateLink traffic never hits the NAT? We want control-plane calls to use the interface endpoint directly.

Mira: Make the interface endpoint subnet have only local routes and security group rules to allow host ENIs. In k8s, ensure DNS resolves to the interface endpoint IPs (VPC DNS + private hosted zone or endpoint DNS). Also, avoid egress policies that force all traffic through a sidecar that SNATs to the node IP — that can route through NAT.

Sam: Cost note: multiple NATs per AZ increases monthly bill. For multiple accounts at scale consider a hub VPC with TGW and centralized NATs, share via TGW attachments. That reduces number of NATs but adds TGW fees — usually cheaper past a certain scale.

Alex: Would TGW + central NAT still work with cross-account PrivateLink? We want to keep endpoints in each spoke for latency, but central egress for internet.

Raj: Yes — interface endpoints stay in each spoke. TGW handles cross-account routing for other services. Watch out for asymmetrical routing for return packets; ensure the return path is via TGW/NAT as expected. Also update security/Audit to reflect cross-account flows.

cloud-ops-bot: Update on case 1234567890: a100 quota increased from 0 -> 20 in eu-west-1. p4d request still pending with support for capacity confirmation.

Alex: Awesome, thanks everyone. Next steps: I'll open the infra PR with: subnet blocks, per-AZ NAT gw design, route tables, and endpoint subnet. Will ping for review once PR is up.

Mira: @Alex ping us when the PR is ready — also include helm/eksctl annotations for nodegroups so we can validate ENI/IP allocation.

Raj: Adding the quota case number to the PR for traceability.

Sam: If you want, I can run a quick cost estimate for NAT options (per-AZ vs central TGW) — say yes and I'll add numbers to the PR. :money_with_wings:

Alex: Yes please — would love a rough monthly delta. Thanks all!
